prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a wide indoor corridor receding from left to right along a slatted wall and storefront glass (1.5 to 8 m away) toward a dark background opening (>10 m away), with a smooth ground gradient and ceiling above. In frames 1 to 3, a person in a pink-striped jacket on the left is brightest and within arm's reach of the camera wearer (0.8 to 1.5 m) before exiting the left edge in frame 4, while two people on the right (in a patterned top at 2 to 2.5 m and a black Adidas hoodie at 1 to 1.5 m) approach and exit the right edge by frame 4. As the foreground clears and the camera wearer advances slightly left, a standing person in a grey jacket on the left (moving from ~2.5 m in frame 1 to ~1.5 m in frame 5, initially occluded by the striped-jacket person), a person seated on the floor against the wall (~3.5 to 3 m away, flanked by low-lying backpacks within their arm's reach), a standing man in dark clothing (~4.5 to 4 m away), and a distant person near the exit (~8 to 10 m away) remain spaced 1 to 4 m apart along the wall. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the continuous metric ordering of the floor plane, the slatted wall versus the recessed glass, and the exact front-to-back layering of overlapping people immediately clear without visual clutter from indoor reflections. However, it provides little detail on facial orientation or fine limb pose (which in RGB show most people facing inward or toward the camera wearer), and it is unreliable on the glass storefront where reflections and interior depth are flattened into a uniform wall plane, as well as on dark floor bags that blend into the ground.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground people and objects against a blacked-out background, tracking their 2D footprints and occlusions from left to right across the corridor. In frames 1 and 2, the large mask of the person in the pink-striped jacket on the left (1 to 1.5 m away, facing away and right) partially occludes the person in the grey jacket behind them (~2.5 m away, within their arm's reach), while on the right the mask of the person in the black hoodie (~1 to 1.5 m away, partly cut off by the right frame edge) overlaps the person in the patterned top (~2 m away, bending downward) before both exit right and the striped-jacket person exits left by frame 4. Midground masks delineate the seated person on the floor (~3 to 3.5 m away) with adjacent backpacks within arm's reach on the ground, the standing man in dark clothing (~4 to 4.5 m away, about 1.5 m to the right of the seated person), a distant pedestrian (~8 to 10 m away), and in frame 5 a cell phone held within the grey-jacketed person's hands (~1.5 m away). This map highlights small ground-level backpacks, the held cell phone, and distant or overlapping silhouettes (such as the sliver of the grey-jacketed person behind the foreground person in frames 1 and 2) that are hard to separate in the busy RGB image. However, the map is unreliable in several places: it completely misses the grey-jacketed person in frame 3, drops the seated person in frames 3 and 5, misclassifies the bending person in the patterned top on the right of frame 3 as a 'dog' and a background pillar reflection as a 'person' in frame 4, and conveys no 3D depth or gaze direction.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map renders sparse 2D joint wireframe locations for only 1 to 2 individuals per frame against a completely black background, omitting all scene layout, objects, and most people present in the RGB strip. In frame 1, a single skeleton on the left captures the person in the pink-striped jacket (~1.5 m away) turned away from the camera wearer in three-quarter rear profile with their left arm bent toward their hip and head angled right. In frame 2, only the standing person in the grey jacket (~2.2 m away on the left) is tracked facing right in profile with elbows bent and hands near waist level, while in frames 4 and 5 their skeleton (~1.5 to 1.8 m away) turns to face the camera wearer with both arms bent inward to hold an object within arm's reach, including magenta hand keypoints in frame 4. In frame 5, a second skeleton appears on the right for the standing man in dark clothing (~4 m away), showing a frontal stance facing toward the camera wearer with arms angled toward his pockets, separated by roughly 2.5 m from the person in grey on the left. While the skeleton map clarifies torso twist, shoulder alignment, and two-handed manipulation for the tracked individuals more explicitly than the RGB frames, it is highly unreliable for overall scene understanding because it fails to detect all other nearby and distant people across all five frames and provides no metric distance or occlusion boundaries.
